# Labour Party Manifesto 2010: Summary

## Core Vision
The 2010 Labour Manifesto, titled "A Future Fair for All," addressed three major crises: the global economic downturn, the political expenses scandal, and ongoing military operations in Afghanistan. It proposed rebuilding the economy, reforming public services, and restoring political trust while protecting fairness.

## Economic Priorities
Labour pledged to halve the deficit by 2014 through economic growth, fair taxation, and spending cuts to lower-priority areas. Key proposals included maintaining public spending during recovery, reforming banking regulations, creating UK Finance for Growth (£4 billion for businesses), investing in high-speed rail and broadband infrastructure, and supporting one million new skilled jobs. The manifesto emphasized long-term industrial strategy, renewable energy investment, and a Green Investment Bank.

## Employment and Welfare
Labour committed to ending long-term unemployment through the Future Jobs Fund, guaranteeing jobs for those unemployed over two years. The National Minimum Wage would rise with average earnings, with a £40-per-week "Better Off in Work" guarantee. Expanded apprenticeships and skills training were promised.

## Public Services
**Education:** Increased spending on Sure Start, schools, and childcare; guaranteed one-to-one tuition for struggling pupils; school choice with underperforming schools subject to takeover; education participation until 18.

**Healthcare:** NHS spending protected with legally binding patient guarantees including 18-week treatment waits, one-week cancer test results, and expanded preventative healthcare. More personal care and home-based services were promised.

## Social Policy
Support for families included a "Father's Month" of flexible leave, Toddler Tax Credit, and extended flexible working rights. A National Care Service would provide free home care for those with greatest needs. The state pension would be re-linked to earnings, with new pension savings schemes.

## Security and Immigration
Police numbers would be maintained with neighbourhood teams. An Australian-style points-based immigration system would control migration. Anti-social behaviour measures would be strengthened.

## Political Reform
Referenda were proposed on Alternative Vote elections and House of Lords reform. Fixed-term parliaments, a written constitution commission, and lobbying regulation were promised to restore political trust.
